extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing the PCT international search and preparing the written opinion and international search report (Form PCT/ISA/210 / PCT/ISA/237) in accordance with the PCT and MPEP. Covers prior art scope, search orientation, excluded subject matter, reporting, form-filling, and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Opinion content (PCT Rule 43 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Searching Authority shall establish a written opinion as to whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step (to be non-obvious), and to be industrially applicable; and whether the international application complies with the requirements of the Treaty and these Regulations in so far as checked by the ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written opinion is established at the same time as the international search report or declaration under Article 17(2)(a). It should also be accompanied by other observations provided for in the Regulations (e.g., clarity of claims, description and drawings, support of claims). Applicable provisions (Articles 33(2)-(6), 35(2)-(3), Rules 43.4, 43.6bis, 64, 65, 66.1(e), etc.) apply mutatis mutandis. If the ISA cannot form a meaningful opinion for certain claims (see Rules 43 bis.1(b), 66.1(e)), it must indicate that in Box No. III of Form PCT/ISA/237.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Relevant Prior Art (PCT Rule 33.1 / Article 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant prior art consists of everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by means of written disclosure (including drawings and other illustrations) capable of assisting in determining novelty and inventive step, provided the making available occurred prior to the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written disclosure is publicly available if the public could access and acquire its contents at the relevant date and no confidentiality bar existed. If only month or year is given, presume last day of month/year unless evidence shows otherwise. Prior art for written opinion uses international filing date or earliest valid priority date per PCT Rule 64.1(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-written disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-written disclosures (oral disclosure, use, exhibition, other non-written means) are not part of prior art for the international search unless substantiated by a written disclosure made available prior to the international filing date; if so, the written disclosure constitutes the prior art and the search report must separately mention the non-written disclosure and its date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international preliminary examination, if a non-written disclosure occurred before the relevant date and its date is indicated in a written disclosure published on or after the relevant date, the non-written disclosure is not considered prior art but must be called to attention in the international preliminary examination report (Rule 64.2; Rule 70.9). For cases where a written disclosure only demonstrates the non-written disclosure date, indicate both facts and dates in the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special mention of published applications/patents with later publication but earlier filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any published application or patent whose publication date is the same as or later than, but whose filing date or claimed priority date is earlier than, the international filing date, and which would have been relevant had it been published before the international filing date, shall be specially mentioned in the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international preliminary examination similar treatment applies: such documents shall not be considered part of prior art under Article 33(2)-(3) if published after the relevant date, but the international preliminary examination report shall call attention to them (Rule 64.3; Rule 70.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields to be covered by the international search (PCT Rule 33.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search shall cover all technical fields and search files which may contain material pertinent to the invention, including not only the art where the invention is classifiable but also analogous arts regardless of where classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine analogous arts in light of the necessary essential function or use of the invention, not only expressly indicated functions. The search should embrace subject matter generally recognized as equivalent to the claimed invention for all or certain features, even if described differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation of the international search (PCT Rule 33.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search shall be made on the basis of the claims, with due regard to the description and drawings, and with particular emphasis on the inventive concept towards which the claims are directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As far as possible and reasonable, the search shall cover the entire subject matter to which the claims are directed or which they might reasonably be expected to be directed after amendment. Focus on claim scope and inventive concept when selecting search fields and terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant date for prior art in international preliminary examination (PCT Rule 64.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of Article 33(2) and (3) the relevant date is generally the international filing date, except where a valid priority is claimed; then the filing date of the earlier application is the relevant date (with specific rules for late international filings within two months of priority expiry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the International Preliminary Examining Authority considers the priority claim invalid, the relevant date may be the international filing date. Carefully verify and record the effective relevant date when assessing prior art for the written opinion and preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet and online disclosures handling (printouts, L-documents, citation categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art disclosures on the Internet or online databases are treated as written disclosures and are considered publicly available as of the date the disclosure was publicly posted; examiners should obtain an electronic document establishing the publication date and make a printout that records the URL and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the printout in the international search report as an “L” document and classify its relevance by content and established date (e.g., “X”, “Y”, “A”, or with prefixes like “P,X”). If publication date cannot be established but the disclosure is relevant to novelty/inventive step, cite it as an L document for the claims it would have affected, using the printout date as its publication date. Treat all websites as non-secure unless a secure/commercial arrangement exists; use secure connections when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners encouraged to cite supportive prior art beyond novelty/inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are encouraged to cite prior art that might assist in determining other requirements (e.g., sufficient support of claims by description, industrial applicability) and documents important for background or showing level of ordinary skill, but should not spend time searching for these unless there is a special reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite documents putting doubt upon validity of priority claims, documents that improve understanding of the invention, or documents illustrating background. Do not expand the search beyond standard parameters solely to find such documents, but cite relevant post-dating documents to show universal facts when appropriate. Be mindful that different designated Offices may have different effective-date definitions and select citations accordingly when reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search resources and minimum documentation (PCT Article 15(4), Rule 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA must endeavor to discover as much relevant prior art as its facilities permit and must consult the so-called 'minimum documentation' and the most relevant search resources for the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use databases listed in the U.S. Search Guidance index and organize search effort and time to minimize the possibility of failing to discover highly relevant prior art (e.g., anticipatory documents). Recognize practical limits (text-search limitations, classification system imperfections) and prioritize search time and resources accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and use of Internet as a search tool
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the Internet for searching unpublished international applications, treat all websites as non-secure unless the Office has a secure commercial arrangement with the service provider; exercise extreme caution to avoid exposing search terms or the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a relevant database is accessible via the Internet but an alternative secure connection exists, use the secure connection. If no secure connection exists, use generalized search terms representing combinations of features already shown to exist in the art to reduce risk of disclosure of search terms or application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter not required to be searched or examined (PCT Rule 39 / 67)
rubrics_metrics.description: No ISA or IPEA shall be required to search or carry out international preliminary examination to the extent the subject matter is: (i) scientific and mathematical theories; (ii) plant/animal varieties or essentially biological processes for producing plants/animals (except microbiological processes and their products); (iii) schemes, rules or methods of doing business, performing purely mental acts or playing games; (iv) methods for treatment by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods; (v) mere presentations of information; (vi) computer programs to the extent the Authority is not equipped to search them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO declares it will search/examine all subject matter searched in U.S. national applications, but applicants should consider which ISA to select. Lack of an international search report for such subject matter does not by itself affect validity or further processing of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: No search when claims/description/drawings are unclear or inadequately supported
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA considers that the description, claims, or drawings fail to comply with prescribed requirements to such an extent that a meaningful search cannot be carried out, it may declare that it will not establish a search report; similarly, if the claims are so unclear or inadequately supported no meaningful opinion can be formed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include missing or non-compliant nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings, improper multiple dependent claims (PCT Rule 6.4(a)), or other deficiencies preventing meaningful assessment of novelty, inventive step, or industrial applicability. In such cases the ISA may not address those issues in its written opinion per Rules 43 bis.1(b) and 66.1(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for claims not searched and for unclear claims (reporting and forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some claims are unsearchable or relate to subject matter the ISA will not search, the ISA searches the remaining claims and indicates any unsearched claims and reasons in Box No. II of Form PCT/ISA/210; if none are searched, the ISA declares no search report established using Form PCT/ISA/203.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application cites an inaccessible document essential to understanding the invention, the ISA may postpone the search and request a copy; if not received, attempt the search then indicate inability or restriction. For written opinion, indicate in Box No. III of Form PCT/ISA/237 that no opinion will be established regarding novelty, inventive step, or industrial applicability for those claims and refer to the search report or declaration for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and publication timing for search report and written opinion (PCT Rule 42.1 / 43 bis.1(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of the international application occurs at 18 months from earliest priority date (or 18 months from filing if no priority). The Office's goal is to have the search report and written opinion mailed so they reach the International Bureau by the end of 16 months from the priority date (or 9 months from filing date if no priority claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after July 1, 2014, the written opinion of the ISA and any informal applicant comments will be made publicly available in their original language at publication. The timing ensures sufficient time for technical publication preparations (by 17.5 months). See PCT Rule 42.1 and 43 bis.1(a) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and limitations of the international search report (PCT Article 18 / Rule 43)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report contains citations of documents considered relevant, the classification of the subject matter, and an indication of the fields searched. The search report records the results (Form PCT/ISA/210) and is transmitted to the applicant and International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations of particular relevance must be specially indicated; citations relevant only to certain claims must be cited in relation to those claims; if only certain passages are relevant, identify page/column/line. The search report should identify prior art only and must not include opinion, reasoning, argument or explanation as to cited prior art — those belong in the written opinion (Form PCT/ISA/237).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing and filling Form PCT/ISA/210 (first sheet boxes and general form rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first sheet indicates the total number of sheets in the report (count only filled-in sheets from Form PCT/ISA/210). Box 1a indicates language of search basis (language filed or English translation), Box 1b indicates rectification of an obvious mistake under PCT Rule 91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter the correct number of sheets (exclude blank sheets). Use the first sheet and available continuation sheets as directed (continuations for nucleotide listings, unsearched claims/unity lack, abstract text, and extra/second-sheet continuation for citations). Follow the July 2022 PCT/ISA/210 variant guidance where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings on forms (Box 1c and continuation sheet use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application discloses nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences, check Box 1c and use Box No. I on 'continuation of first sheet (1)' to indicate whether the sequence listing was filed as part of the international application or later, whether accompanied by required statements, and whether a meaningful search could be carried out without an ST.26-compliant listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize whether the listing was filed with the application or subsequently, whether it complies with required statements (does not go beyond disclosure), indicate if the report was established to the extent that a meaningful search could be carried out without ST.26 compliance, and include any additional comments on Item 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which parts of the international search report are published and continuation-sheet usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the 'second sheet', the 'continuation of second sheet', the 'continuation of first sheet (2)' (if any), the 'extra sheet' (if any), and any separate sheet with patent family information are published by the International Bureau; the 'first sheet' and some continuation first sheets contain information already on the front page of the published international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific continuation sheets for their intended purposes: continuation of first sheet (1) for sequence listings and search basis, continuation of first sheet (2) when claims were found unsearchable or unity lacking, continuation of first sheet (3) for the abstract text, and continuation of second sheet for additional citations when space is insufficient. The patent family annex is not currently used by the U.S. ISA.
